newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices mostly softer on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices mostly softer on mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly lower Thursday as above-normal temperatures were forecast for the U.S. through the weekend, industry sources said.
Swing Gulf Coast prices were talked in the $2.45-2.60 per mmBtu range, down about $1.30 from January indices, but mostly steady from Tuesday's notional values.
However, a return of significant industrial loads after the holiday gave some support to the Gulf Coast market, sources said.
At the New York city-gate, prices fell by about 10-20 cents to the $3.40-3.60 range, with late offers heard as low as $3.35.
Temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic states are expected to remain above-normal through at least the weekend, with some cooler air forecast to roll in early next week.
In response to the mild weather in the central U.S., Midcontinent prices plummeted to about $2.30, down about 60 cents from Tuesday's price discussion and down nearly $2 from January indices.
Temperatures throughout most of the Midwest are forecast to remain about 10 degrees above-normal through Saturday, with temperatures as much as 25 degrees above-normal possible.
In west Texas, where temperatures are about 15-25 degrees above-normal, Permian gas prices fell into the high-$2.20s, down almost 20 cents from Tuesday.
Similarly at the southern California border, deals were reported done about 15 cents lower around $2.40, falling almost $2 under January's index.
